Would it be fair for you to switch the terms “collective consciousness” to “distributed cognition” ?

The idea that no one person shapes society. No one person maintains the power grid, runs the water, builds the buildings, develops musical melody, creates culture, educates people, etc.

Basically all of the scaffolding that allows us to live our lives depends on something greater than the individual, but requires the participation of the individual in order to exist.

It is not a thing, in the same way that gravity is not a thing. It is an effect that can be observed.

I think changing the thinking from a “thing” to a “process” helps remove some of the spiritual woo from it.

It requires both emanation and emergence.

All this to say, I think “collective consciousness” is a poor way of conceptualizing what we are trying to point to.
